name: Sermorelin
status: Not currently FDA-approved: Geref was approved in 1990 and 1997, discontinued in 2008; compounded versions are unapproved
mechanism: The first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone, which tell the pituitary to release growth hormone in pulses

article.summary: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of GHRH. The FDA approved it as Geref until the maker discontinued it in 2008; today compounding pharmacies sell it for anti-aging with limited adult evidence.
article.takeaway: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), enough to prompt the pituitary to release growth hormone. The FDA approved it as Geref in 1990 (as a diagnostic test) and in 1997 (for children with idiopathic growth hormone deficiency); the maker discontinued it in 2008, and the FDA later determined this was not for safety or effectiveness reasons.[^1] It sped growth in GH-deficient children,[^2] but evidence for adult anti-aging use is limited to small studies of related analogs.[^3] Compounding pharmacies now supply unapproved versions, and WADA bans sermorelin.[^4]
glance: Not currently approved; Geref was approved in 1990 and 1997 and discontinued in 2008[^1]
Anti-aging, body composition, sleep, GH support
Injection under the skin (compounded products); no approved current dosing
Pediatric trials; small adult studies of GHRH analogs[^2][^3]
Prohibited at all times; WADA names sermorelin[^4]

blocks.text: The hypothalamus releases GHRH in pulses, and each pulse triggers a burst of growth hormone from the pituitary. Sermorelin copies the first 29 amino acids of GHRH, the shortest synthetic piece that keeps full biological activity.[^5] Because it works through the pituitary's own control system, the body's feedback loops still operate, which is the main argument for using it instead of injecting growth hormone. Long-term comparisons between the two are lacking.

rows: Height velocity rose from 4.1 to about 7.2 cm per year; well tolerated[^2]
Skin thickness rose in both sexes; lean mass, insulin sensitivity and well-being improved in men only; the only adverse effect was a temporary rise in blood fats[^3]
Better scores on several cognitive tests than placebo[^6]

blocks.text: The adult studies were small, short and used GHRH analogs. They do not show that compounded sermorelin changes how older adults feel, function or live.

items: **Pediatric record:** in the year-long Geref trial there were no adverse changes in routine blood and hormone tests, no change in fasting glucose and no excessive IGF-1[^2]
**Adults:** the studies lasted only 4 to 6 months, so the effects of years of raised IGF-1 on cancer, heart disease or survival are unknown[^3][^6]
**Mixed benefit:** in the adult trial, benefits seen in men did not appear in women[^3]
**Quality:** compounded and gray-market products are not FDA-reviewed for quality; illegally sold peptide drugs have shown low purity and toxic metals[^7]

blocks.text: Geref was approved in the US in 1990 (diagnostic use) and 1997 (children with idiopathic GH deficiency). EMD Serono discontinued it in 2008, and in 2013 the FDA determined it had not been withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness.[^1] A DailyMed search found no current FDA label for any sermorelin product; compounding pharmacies supply unapproved versions.
WADA lists sermorelin as a prohibited GHRH analog at all times.[^4]

Sermorelin has a real history as an approved pediatric drug, but the anti-aging claims rest on small adult studies of related molecules. Its long-term safety in healthy adults is unknown. Athletes subject to drug testing should treat it as banned.

evidence.label: Moderate for children; thin for adult anti-aging
evidence.text: Pediatric trials supported the old approval, though the key one was open label.[^2] Adult studies are small, short and used related analogs.[^3][^6]

faq.q: Why did Geref disappear from the market?
faq.a: EMD Serono discontinued it in 2008, and the FDA later found it was not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons.[^1]

faq.q: Is sermorelin the same as tesamorelin?
faq.a: No. Both are GHRH analogs, but [tesamorelin](/peptides/tesamorelin) is a stabilized analog approved for HIV-related belly fat, while sermorelin is the plain 1-29 fragment.
Yes. WADA lists sermorelin among prohibited GHRH analogs at all times.[^4]
